entities.name: PMID:25090481
observations: Zozulińska-Ziółkiewicz et al. studied 79 people with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes in the Poznan Prospective Study.
Participants completed a structured 5-day education program and a 20-question diabetes-knowledge test, followed for 11 years.
The paper reports baseline diabetic knowledge as an independent predictor of subclinical macroangiopathy.

entities.name: Type 1 diabetes
observations: The study population consisted of people with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes receiving intensive functional insulin therapy from diagnosis.

entities.name: Knowledge predicts carotid IMT
observations: In 79 participants followed for 11 years, baseline diabetes knowledge was inversely correlated with right common carotid intima-media thickness (r = -0.27, p = 0.017).

Multivariable linear regression adjusted for sex, age, smoking, hypertension, diabetic kidney disease, mean follow-up LDL cholesterol, and HbA1c; knowledge remained associated with IMT (β = -8, 95% CI -16 to -1, p = 0.037).

entities.name: Subclinical macroangiopathy
observations: Subclinical macroangiopathy was assessed by right common carotid artery intima-media thickness using high-resolution ultrasonography and automated Carotid Analyzer for Research software.
At 11 years, median carotid IMT was 560 μm (IQR 520–630).
